knowledge_point.title: Integrating an Algebraic Function With Positive Integer Exponent

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=3x-7.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 48(3x-7)^{7}\,\text{d}x & =\int 48{u}^{7}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =48\cdot \frac{1}{3}\int {u}^{7}\,\text{d}u \\  & =16\cdot \frac{{u}^{8}}{8}+C \\  & =2\cdot {u}^{8}+C \\  & =2(3x-7)^{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[2(3x-7)^{8}+C] & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[2(3x-7)^{8}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =16(3x-7)^{7}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x-7)+0 \\  & =16(3x-7)^{7}\cdot 3 \\  & =48(3x-7)^{7}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: All real x; C an arbitrary integration constant.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=12-5x.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-5\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{5}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 18(12-5x)^{5}\,\text{d}x & =\int 18{u}^{5}\cdot (-\frac{1}{5})\text{d}u \\  & =18\cdot (-\frac{1}{5})\int {u}^{5}\cdot \,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{18}{5}\int {u}^{5}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{18}{5}\cdot \frac{{u}^{6}}{6}+C \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}{u}^{6}+C \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}(12-5x)^{6}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[-\frac{3}{5}(12-5x)^{6}+C] & =-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{3}{5}(12-5x)^{6}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =-\frac{18}{5}(12-5x)^{5}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(12-5x)+0 \\  & =-\frac{18}{5}(12-5x)^{5}\cdot (-5) \\  & =18(12-5x)^{5}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
